claim: Recent studies using high-dimensional single-cell profiling technologies have identified subsets of synovial monocytes/macrophages.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: One RA synovial macrophage subset, termed cluster 1, was increased in RA relative to osteoarthritis samples.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: ICI-arthritis synovial fluid contains elevated levels of IL-1β, IL-6, IFN-γ, and IL-17A.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Co-stimulation of monocytes with PGE2+TNF induced expression of genes enriched in inflammatory and NF-κB pathways.
source: As expected, co-stimulation of monocytes with PGE2+TNF induced expression of genes enriched in inflammatory and NF-κB pathways, largely reflecting a TNF response (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: PGE2 suppresses expression of a subset of TNF-inducible genes including TNF itself and interferon-stimulated genes CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11.
source: Clustering of genes upregulated after 3 hr of stimulation (n=747; fold change >2, false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.05) based upon pattern of expression confirmed that PGE2 suppresses expression of a subset of TNF-inducible genes including TNF itself and interferon-stimulated genes CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCL11 (Figure 1C, group III, n=86 suppressed genes).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PGE2 augmented TNF-mediated induction of 395 genes.
source: Surprisingly, PGE2 augmented TNF-mediated induction of a substantially larger number of genes (Figure 1C, groups I and V, 395 co-stimulated genes).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Genes costimulated by PGE2+TNF were enriched in inflammatory pathways (e.g., response to lipopolysaccharide, neutrophil migration).
source: Pathway analysis revealed that genes costimulated by PGE2+TNF were similarly enriched in inflammatory pathways (e.g., response to lipopolysaccharide, neutrophil migration), although the enriched pathways were partially distinct (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's pathway analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: PGE2 alone induced canonical cAMP signaling and CREB target genes such as HBEGF and CREM.
source: We also observed two groups of genes that were induced by PGE2 alone, which included canonical cAMP signaling and CREB target genes (Zhang et al., 2005) such as HBEGF and CREM (Figure 1C, groups II and IV).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PGE2 inhibits TNF-induced expression of cholesterol pathway genes.
source: Analysis of RNAseq performed at the 24 hr time point to determine the effects of PGE2 on the late phase TNF response showed similar results and additionally revealed that PGE2 inhibits TNF-induced expression of cholesterol pathway genes, which we had previously shown to be induced by TNF with delayed kinetics and to play a role in promoting IFN responses (Kusnadi et al., 2019; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes recapitulated 61% of fibroblast-augmented TNF-inducible genes.
source: Strikingly, (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes recapitulated 61% of fibroblast-augmented TNF-inducible genes (Figure 2A, hypergeometric p=8.36e-128), which is in accord with our previous conclusions that PGE2 mediates a substantial fraction of the fibroblast effect on monocytes (Kuo et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's comparative analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes highly significantly mimicked the RA C1 phenotype (p<10e-9 by Monte Carlo simulation).
source: Strikingly, (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes (Figure 2B, orange+yellow) highly significantly mimicked the RA C1 phenotype (p<10e-9 by Monte Carlo simulation) and recapitulated the C1 phenotype more completely than TNF/fibroblast-costimulated genes (Figure 2B, orange+red).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's comparative analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes were parts of pathogenic gene modules related to IL-1-NF-κB and Jak-STAT signaling, neutrophil chemotaxis, and the Notch pathway.
source: The (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes were parts of pathogenic gene modules related to IL-1-NF-κB and Jak-STAT signaling, neutrophil chemotaxis, and the Notch pathway that has been recently implicated in RA pathogenesis (Wei et al., 2020; Zack et al., 2024; Figure 2C, blue font = C1 genes).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's pathway analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cluster 4 of ICI-arthritis myeloid cells, accounting for 15% of cells, selectively showed elevated expression of (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes and known PGE2 targets.
source: Cluster 4, accounting for 15% of cells, selectively showed elevated expression of (TNF+PGE2)-costimulated genes and known PGE2 targets, including HBEGF, IL1B, CXCL2/3/8, CREM, and PLAUR (Figure 2F, genes marked in red).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The majority of ICI-arthritis myeloid cells mapped onto four RA myeloid clusters: IL1B + FCN1 + HBEGF+, STAT1+ CXCL10+, SPP1+, and MERTK+ HBEGF+ clusters.
source: Reference mapping (Hao et al., 2024; Lotfollahi et al., 2024) showed that the majority of ICI-arthritis myeloid cells mapped onto four RA myeloid clusters: IL1B + FCN1 + HBEGF+, STAT1+ CXCL10+, SPP1+, and MERTK+ HBEGF+ clusters (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's reference mapping analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Expression of the TP signature in RA myeloid cells aligned most closely with the IL1B+ FCN1+ HBEGF+ cluster.
source: Analysis of RA myeloid cells showed that expression of the TP genes aligned most closely with the IL1B+ FCN1+ HBEGF+ cluster, although gene expression extended into subsets of adjacent SPP1+, MERTK+ LYVE1-, and DC2 clusters (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's gene set activity analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The TP signature was absent from the IFN signature-expressing STAT1+ CXCL10+ cells in RA.
source: Notably, the TP signature was absent from the IFN signature-expressing STAT1+ CXCL10+ cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's gene set activity analysis.

claim: Selective agonists of EP2 and EP4 augmented TNF-induced expression of IL1B, IL1A, STAT4, and CXCL1.
source: Selective agonists of EP2 and EP4 augmented TNF-induced expression of IL1B, IL1A, STAT4, and CXCL1, while suppressing induction of the ISG CXCL10 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Selective agonists of EP2 and EP4 suppressed induction of the ISG CXCL10.
source: Selective agonists of EP2 and EP4 augmented TNF-induced expression of IL1B, IL1A, STAT4, and CXCL1, while suppressing induction of the ISG CXCL10 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Dibutyryl-cAMP augmented TNF-induced expression of IL1B, IL1A, STAT4, and CXCL1, while suppressing induction of CXCL10.
source: Dibutyryl-cAMP showed similar results (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: cAMP signaling is implicated in both anti- and pro-inflammatory effects in this experimental system.
source: These results implicate cAMP signaling in both anti- and pro-inflammatory effects in this experimental system.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings with EP2/EP4 agonists and dibutyryl-cAMP.

claim: TNF and PGE2 induced mostly distinct ATACseq peaks.
source: In accord with different signaling pathways activated by these factors, TNF and PGE2 induced mostly distinct ATACseq peaks (Figure 5A); indeed, out of 15,190 induced ATACseq peaks (FDR < 0.05, fold induction >2), only 1547 peaks (10.2%) were commonly induced by individual stimulation by TNF or PGE2 (Figure 5A, columns 4+7).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's ATACseq analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: TF binding motifs most significantly enriched under TNF-induced ATACseq peaks corresponded to AP-1 and NF-κB binding sites.
source: As expected, TF binding motifs most significantly enriched under TNF-induced ATACseq peaks corresponded to AP-1 and NF-κB binding sites; additional enriched motifs included RUNX and IRF1 sites, the latter of which is in accord with the role of IRF1 in the delayed TNF-induced autocrine IFN response (Yarilina et al., 2008; Figure 5B, left).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: PGE2 induced peaks enriched for AP-1 motifs and additionally induced peaks with highly significant enrichment of CEBPD and NR4A1 motifs.
source: Similar to TNF, PGE2 induced peaks enriched for AP-1 motifs and additionally induced peaks with highly significant enrichment of CEBPD and NR4A1 motifs (Figure 5B, middle), which is in accord with PGE2-mediated induction of expression of TFs belonging to these three TF families (Altarejos and Montminy, 2011; Zhang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: TNF and PGE2 cooperated to increase chromatin accessibility at co-induced peaks.
source: TNF and PGE2 cooperated to increase chromatin accessibility at co-induced peaks (Figure 5C, upper), and the most significantly enriched motifs were AP-1 (Fra1, also known as FOSL1) and CEBPE (Figure 5C, lower).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's ATACseq analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The most significantly enriched motifs at co-induced peaks were AP-1 (Fra1, also known as FOSL1) and CEBPE.
source: TNF and PGE2 cooperated to increase chromatin accessibility at co-induced peaks (Figure 5C, upper), and the most significantly enriched motifs were AP-1 (Fra1, also known as FOSL1) and CEBPE (Figure 5C, lower).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The peaks that were uniquely induced by PGE2+TNF were most significantly enriched for AP-1, CEBP, and ISRE/IRF motifs.
source: The peaks that were uniquely induced by PGE2+TNF were most significantly enriched for AP-1, CEBP, and ISRE/IRF motifs, and also for GAPBA, KLF7, and PBX1 binding sites (Figure 5B, right, and data not shown), and were associated with immune response and cytokine genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ChromVAR analysis showed that, relative to TNF alone, the PGE2+TNF costimulation condition was characterized by increased AP-1 and CEBP activity, and also NR4A1 activity.
source: This analysis reinforced the notion that, relative to TNF alone, the PGE2+TNF costimulation condition was characterized by increased AP-1 and CEBP activity, and also NR4A1 activity.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's ChromVAR analysis.

claim: A direct pairwise comparison of T+P to T revealed the most significant increases in AP-1 and CEBP occupancy.
source: A direct pairwise comparison of T+P to T revealed the most significant increases in AP-1 and CEBP occupancy (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's TOBIAS analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: IFN-γ essentially completely abolished induction of inflammatory genes IL1B and CXCL2, and the Notch target gene HEY1.
source: Surprisingly, IFN-γ essentially completely abolished induction of inflammatory genes IL1B and CXCL2, and the Notch target gene HEY1 (Figure 6A); as a specificity control, induction of STAT4 was minimally affected.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: IFN-γ suppressed expression of approximately 27% of genes that were most clearly synergistically induced by (T+P).
source: Interestingly, IFN-γ suppressed expression of only approximately 27% of genes that were most clearly synergistically induced by (T+P) (Figure 6B; this group included IL-1 pathway genes NLRP3 and PTGS2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: IFN-γ suppressed induction of IL-1 family members IL1B and IL1A, neutrophil chemokine genes CXCL1/2/3/5/8, and canonical cAMP signaling targets such as EREG and NR4A1/3.
source: Similarly, IFN-γ suppressed induction of only a subset of additional genes that were costimulated by (T+P) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C; these suppressed genes included IL-1 family members IL1B and IL1A, neutrophil chemokine genes CXCL1/2/3/5/8, and canonical cAMP signaling targets such as EREG and NR4A1/3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Genes more highly expressed under IFN-γ-stimulated conditions included inflammatory genes such as TNF and ISGs such as CXCL10.
source: This opposition between IFN-γ and PGE2 was also apparent in the regulation of a subset of TNF-induced genes that were suppressed by PGE2, whose expression was substantially higher under IFN-γ-stimulated conditions (Figure 6C and D). Genes more highly expressed under IFN-γ-stimulated conditions included inflammatory genes such as TNF and ISGs such as CXCL10.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: IFN-γ inhibits select inflammatory pathways while promoting others.
source: Collectively, the results support a biology whereby PGE2 and IFN-γ at least in part oppose each other by regulating TNF-induced gene expression in different directions and suggest that IFN-γ inhibits select inflammatory pathways while promoting others.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: IFN-γ minimally affected the (T+P)-induced NF-κB response.
source: Interestingly, IFN-γ minimally affected the (T+P)-induced NF-κB response (IC4).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's interaction analysis.

claim: IFN-γ regulates the PGE2 response, at least in part by modulating PGE2-induced AP-1 and CEBP factors.
source: Overall, the interaction analysis indicates that IFN-γ does not alter the core NF-κB response (which is activated primarily by TNF) and suggests that instead IFN-γ regulates the PGE2 response, at least in part by modulating PGE2-induced AP-1 and CEBP factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's interaction analysis.

claim: IFN-γ broadly suppresses the PGE2 response, including genes important in RA pathogenesis.
source: Thus, IFN-γ broadly suppresses the PGE2 response, including genes important in RA pathogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's RNAseq analysis.

claim: IFN-γ suppressed 1765 out of 2411 (72%) of PGE2-induced ATACseq peaks.
source: IFN-γ suppressed 1765 out of 2411 (72%) of PGE2-induced ATACseq peaks (Figure 8C, column G2 depicts suppressed peaks).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's ATACseq analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: IFN-γ-suppressed peaks were most significantly enriched in AP-1 and CEBP motifs.
source: These IFN-γ-suppressed peaks were most significantly enriched in AP-1 and CEBP motifs (Figure 8D; the most significantly enriched motif TGAGTCA closely resembles an AP-1 site).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's de novo motif analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claim: ChromVAR analysis confirmed that PGE2 induced AP-1 activity, and this activity was suppressed by IFN-γ.
source: ChromVAR analysis confirmed that PGE2 induced AP-1 activity, and this activity was suppressed by IFN-γ (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's ChromVAR analysis shown in Figure 8E.

claim: NR4A1/2, NFE2L2, and MAF activity was induced by PGE2 and suppressed by IFN-γ.
source: Additionally, NR4A1/2, NFE2L2, and MAF activity was induced by PGE2 and suppressed by IFN-γ.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's ChromVAR analysis.

claim: PGE2 and IFN-γ both induced and repressed different members of the CEBP TF family, with coordinate induction of CEBPB, but opposing regulation of CEBPA, CEBPD, and CEBPE.
source: Remarkably, at the mRNA expression level, PGE2 and IFN-γ both induced and repressed different members of the CEBP TF family, with coordinate induction of CEBPB, but opposing regulation of CEBPA, CEBPD, and CEBPE (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Direct comparison of IFN-γ+PGE2 relative to PGE2 alone using TOBIAS showed striking suppression of AP-1 occupancy.
source: Direct comparison of IFN-γ+PGE2 relative to PGE2 alone using TOBIAS showed striking suppression of AP-1 occupancy and further supported IFN-γ-mediated suppression of NR4A2, NFE2L2, and MAF (Figure 8H).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's TOBIAS analysis shown in Figure 8H.

claim: IFN-γ inhibits PGE2 responses by suppressing AP-1 and a PGE2-induced transcriptional program mediated by AP-1, NR4A1/2, NFE2L2, and MAF TFs.
source: Collectively, these results show that IFN-γ inhibits PGE2 responses by suppressing AP-1 and a PGE2-induced transcriptional program mediated by AP-1, NR4A1/2, NFE2L2, and MAF TFs, and suggest that IFN-γ and PGE2 costimulation remodels the composition and genomic binding profile of CEBP proteins to be distinct from that induced by each stimulus alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: IFN-γ and PGE2 costimulation remodels the composition and genomic binding profile of CEBP proteins to be distinct from that induced by each stimulus alone.
source: Collectively, these results show that IFN-γ inhibits PGE2 responses by suppressing AP-1 and a PGE2-induced transcriptional program mediated by AP-1, NR4A1/2, NFE2L2, and MAF TFs, and suggest that IFN-γ and PGE2 costimulation remodels the composition and genomic binding profile of CEBP proteins to be distinct from that induced by each stimulus alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The TP signature is expressed in an IL1β+ FCN1+ HBEGF+ subset of RA monocytes.
source: We have also found that the TP signature is expressed in an IL1β+ FCN1+ HBEGF+ subset of RA monocytes defined in a more recent study with larger cell numbers that subclustered RA myeloid cells at a higher resolution of 15 clusters (Zhang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of published RA scRNAseq data.

claim: The TP signature may identify one functional phenotype of synovial monocyte that was not well captured by the clustering as performed in Zhang et al., 2023.
source: Alternatively, the TP signature may identify one functional phenotype of synovial monocyte that was not well captured by the clustering as performed in Zhang et al., 2023.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings.

claim: The IL1β+ FCN1+ HBEGF+ cells are essentially devoid of ISG expression.
source: This prediction was indeed borne out, as the IL1β+ FCN1+ HBEGF+ cells are essentially devoid of ISG expression (Zhang et al., 2023; https://immunogenomics.io), and STAT1+ CXCL10+ ISG-hi cells did not express TP genes (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis of published RA scRNAseq data.

claim: STAT1+ CXCL10+ ISG-hi cells did not express TP genes.
source: This prediction was indeed borne out, as the IL1β+ FCN1+ HBEGF+ cells are essentially devoid of ISG expression (Zhang et al., 2023; https://immunogenomics.io), and STAT1+ CXCL10+ ISG-hi cells did not express TP genes (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Colocalization of monocytes with either T cells or with fibroblasts can determine IFN versus TP phenotype.
source: As synovial IFN-γ is made predominantly by T cells and PGE2 by fibroblasts, this suggests that colocalization of monocytes with either T cells (e.g., in lymphoid aggregates) or with fibroblasts (e.g., in synovial lining) can determine IFN versus TP phenotype.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings.

claim: Major sources of PGE2 in inflammatory arthritis and tumors are stromal cells such as fibroblasts and tumor cells.
source: Major sources of PGE2 in inflammatory arthritis and tumors are stromal cells such as fibroblasts and tumor cells (Bayerl et al., 2023; Gong et al., 2023; Kawahara et al., 2015; Kuo et al., 2019; Tsuge et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Macrophages in tissue niches characterized by interaction with fibroblasts will strongly express the PGE2-driven gene expression program including expression of EGFR and Notch ligands that activate fibroblasts.
source: This argues that macrophages in tissue niches characterized by interaction with fibroblasts will strongly express the PGE2-driven gene expression program including expression of EGFR and Notch ligands that activate fibroblasts, suggestive of a positive feedback loop.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings.

claim: IL-1 action on myeloid cells strongly induces COX2 and thus PG production, and an autocrine IL-1-PGE2 loop can further amplify the TP response.
source: IL-1 action on myeloid cells strongly induces COX2 and thus PG production, and an autocrine IL-1-PGE2 loop can further amplify the TP response, as shown in pancreatic tumors (Caronni et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The major sources of IFN-γ in RA are T cells.
source: In contrast, the major sources of IFN-γ in RA are T cells, which are localized either to ectopic germinal center-like structures or are dispersed throughout inflamed synovium (Gravallese and Firestein, 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: IFN-γ is highly expressed by CD8+T cells in ICI-arthritis.
source: IFN-γ is also highly expressed by CD8+T cells in ICI-arthritis (Kim et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: IFN-γ-exposed macrophages express T cell chemokines such as CXCL10 instead of neutrophil chemokines.
source: IFN-γ-exposed macrophages express T cell chemokines such as CXCL10 instead of neutrophil chemokines, thereby promoting T cell-mediated pathogenesis instead of stromal-neutrophil mediated pathogenic responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Distinct subsets of RA patients may exhibit fibroblast/PGE2 versus T cell/IFN-γ-dominant phenotypes and thus be differentially responsive to therapeutics.
source: Distinct subsets of RA patients may exhibit fibroblast/PGE2 versus T cell/IFN-γ-dominant phenotypes and thus be differentially responsive to therapeutics.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings.

claim: In RA, macrophages are major producers of TNF.
source: In RA, macrophages are major producers of TNF, which is a well-established therapeutic target.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: Only a subset of RA patients show >50% improvement after TNF blockade therapy.
source: However, only a subset of RA patients show >50% improvement after TNF blockade therapy, and even these patients can become resistant to therapy (Perera et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: IL-6 blockade therapy is highly effective in a subset of RA patients.
source: While IL-6 blockade therapy is highly effective in a subset of RA patients, IL-1 blockade with anakinra, although an FDA-approved therapy for RA that is effective at suppressing tissue degradation, appears to have limited efficacy in suppressing inflammatory symptoms.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: IL-1 blockade with anakinra is an FDA-approved therapy for RA that is effective at suppressing tissue degradation.
source: While IL-6 blockade therapy is highly effective in a subset of RA patients, IL-1 blockade with anakinra, although an FDA-approved therapy for RA that is effective at suppressing tissue degradation, appears to have limited efficacy in suppressing inflammatory symptoms.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: IL-1 blockade with anakinra appears to have limited efficacy in suppressing inflammatory symptoms.
source: While IL-6 blockade therapy is highly effective in a subset of RA patients, IL-1 blockade with anakinra, although an FDA-approved therapy for RA that is effective at suppressing tissue degradation, appears to have limited efficacy in suppressing inflammatory symptoms.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claim: Interrupting the IL-1-PGE2 axis using IL-1 blockade may release genes such as TNF and CXCL10 from suppression and result in the emergence of stronger TNF- and lymphocyte-driven pathogenic pathways that maintain synovitis.
source: Alternatively, our work raises the intriguing possibility that interrupting the IL-1-PGE2 axis using IL-1 blockade will release genes such as TNF and CXCL10 from suppression and result in the emergence of stronger TNF- and lymphocyte-driven pathogenic pathways that maintain synovitis.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings.
